key_insight: WOVEN shows that many multimodal LLM failures in spatial, physical, embodied, and temporal reasoning can be traced to a shared deficit in visual transition reasoning, which can be trained as a reusable foundation skill.
engineering_relevance: For model builders, the paper suggests a practical recipe for improving MLLMs: train on transition-centric supervision to boost transfer across many downstream vision-language tasks and reduce reliance on task-specific data.
method: Built WOVEN, a 36,076-example benchmark/training set organized by scene, action, and reasoning type across 20 scene types, 5 action types, and 8 reasoning types.
Evaluated 38 frontier MLLMs to measure visual transition reasoning deficits against humans and across model families/scales.
Fine-tuned MLLMs at multiple scales and tested transfer to 26 external benchmarks, plus data substitution experiments and controlled ablations to derive a training recipe.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that even the strongest models fall far below humans, while WOVEN-trained subsets of about 2,000 items each improved 22 of 26 external benchmarks by up to 27.3 percentage points and could replace 30–50% of task-specific data.
watch_item: Because WOVEN uses rollout-based synthetic visual transitions from generative models, transfer gains may depend on rollout realism and may not fully capture all real-world physical dynamics or deployment settings.
paper_title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
